segments.t: In the corridor outside the bustling kitchen, Chef Viktor Petrovich overhears Max speaking about Victoria. Stunned by what he hears, the head chef immediately grabs the bewildered young cook and marches him into his private office for an urgent confrontation. Let us listen to their tense exchange in Russian first.
Пойдём со мной в мой кабинет.
Заходи в комнату и закрой дверь.
Сядь на стул и слушай меня.
Now let us examine the dialogue between Chef Viktor and Max line by line.
Пойдём со мной в мой кабинет.
'Come with me into my office.' Chef Barinov leads with the direct command form meaning 'let us go', followed by 'office'.
'Chef, where are we going now?' Here Max anchors the line on the word meaning 'where' and builds the thought around 'now' and 'are going'.
'We need a very serious conversation.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'necessary' directly with 'very', pairing it with 'serious' and 'conversation'.
'Did you hear everything in the kitchen?' Max turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'heard', followed by 'kitchen'.
'I heard every word of yours.' Notice how naturally this everyday Russian phrase expresses the speaker's point.
'I myself do not understand anything.' Max delivers a punchy conversational reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'understand'.
'You caused a real big scandal.' Chef Barinov uses the action verb meaning 'caused' to focus on the single completed result, pairing it with 'real' and 'big'.
'I did not want to offend anyone.' Notice how naturally this everyday Russian phrase expresses the speaker's point.
Заходи в комнату и закрой дверь.
'Go into the room and close the door.' Chef Barinov leads with the direct command form meaning 'step in', pairing it with 'room' and 'close'.
'Good, I am already closing the door.' Here Max anchors the line on the word meaning 'fine' and builds the thought around 'already' and 'am closing'.
Сядь на стул и слушай меня.
'Sit on a chair and listen to me.' Chef Barinov leads with the direct command form meaning 'sit down', pairing it with 'chair' and 'listen to'.
'I am listening to you attentively, chef.' Max expresses this naturally by combining the word for 'attentively' with 'am listening to'.

'Now your life will change greatly.' Chef Barinov puts the word for 'now' together with 'life' and 'greatly' in a crisp, natural spoken turn of phrase. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.
Пойдём со мной в мой кабинет.
Заходи в комнату и закрой дверь.
Сядь на стул и слушай меня.

With the office door firmly shut, Viktor Petrovich prepares to give Max a stern lecture on family responsibilities and the chaotic consequences of his actions. Next time you watch the episode, listen for the Russian expressions for 'big' and 'carefully' — you will catch every word right away. See you next time!
